extracted.intended_audience: general readers, science-fiction/fantasy readers, and authors researching Clarkesworld Magazine
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarizing Clarkesworld Magazine's history, formats, staff, notable published content, awards, and notable editorial/publishing actions. Useful for readers and authors wanting an overview of the magazine's practices and reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format availability / publication formats
rubrics_metrics.description: All fiction is collected annually in print anthologies published by Wyrm Publishing. Apps are available for Android, iPad and iPhone devices. EPUB, Amazon Kindle, and Mobipocket ebook editions of each issue are available for purchase. All content is available online via the magazine website. All fiction is available in audio format via podcast or direct download. Ebook subscriptions for the Kindle and EPUB readers. Print issues are sold on Amazon and also available as a Patreon subscription option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarkesworld distributes fiction across multiple formats (online, audio/podcast, ebooks, apps, annual print anthologies, and print sales via Amazon/Patreon). For contributors and readers this implies the magazine expects stories to be publishable in text and audio forms and supports multiple delivery channels; no specific formatting rules are listed on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on AI-generated submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: On 20 February 2023, Clarkesworld temporarily closed submissions due to a sudden increase in AI-generated stories sent to the magazine. During the first weeks of 2023, the magazine received 35 times as many fake spam submissions (the magazine categorizes AI-generated stories as spam) as it did last year during the same time frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine treats AI-generated stories as spam and has taken operational steps (temporary closure of submissions) in response to large volumes of such content. For prospective submitters, sending AI-generated work is categorized as spam and will not be accepted; the page does not list a formal submission policy text but the historical action signals strict non-acceptance of AI-produced spam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation initiatives / acceptance of translated works
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarkesworld began a relationship with Storycom in January 2015 to regularly translate and publish works of Chinese science fiction. In February 2019, the editor announced a grant from LTI Korea to translate and publish nine Korean science fiction stories. In November 2022 the magazine announced it would open a submission period for science fiction written in Spanish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine actively commissions or accepts translated works and has run programs/partnerships and grant-funded initiatives to publish translated science fiction from Chinese, Korean, and Spanish-language authors. This indicates an editorial openness to translations and an infrastructure for translated content, though specific submission rules for translations are not provided on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication frequency / schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarkesworld released its first issue October 1, 2006, and has maintained a regular monthly schedule since.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine operates on a monthly publication cadence. Contributors and editors can expect regular monthly issues; the page does not provide deadline or turnaround-time standards but emphasizes consistent monthly output as an operational standard.
